Elections are national elections from Wikipedia's national electoral calendars; dates can change. Disputed areas use Natural Earth's boundaries (disputes_geo.json).

disputes.name: Kashmir
disputes.text: Since 1947 India and Pakistan have both claimed the whole of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir, and fought wars over it in 1947, 1965 and 1999. India controls the south and east, Pakistan the north and west (Gilgit-Baltistan and Azad Kashmir); the 'Line of Control' between them is not an agreed border. China controls Aksai Chin and the Shaksgam Valley, which India also claims. The Siachen Glacier is held by India and claimed by Pakistan.

disputes.name: India–China border (Arunachal Pradesh and others)
disputes.text: India and China have never agreed their Himalayan border, the 'Line of Actual Control'. China claims Arunachal Pradesh (which it calls South Tibet) and several valleys further west, all run by India. The two countries fought a war in 1962, and soldiers died in clashes in the Galwan Valley in 2020.

disputes.name: Western Sahara
disputes.who: Morocco and the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic (Polisario Front)
disputes.text: A former Spanish colony. When Spain left in 1975–76, Morocco took most of it; the Polisario Front, which wants independence for the Sahrawi people, declared the Sahrawi Arab Democratic Republic and fought Morocco until a 1991 ceasefire. Morocco runs about three-quarters of the land, behind a long defensive wall (the 'berm'). The UN lists it as a non-self-governing territory; a promised referendum on independence has never been held.

disputes.name: Palestine: the West Bank (with East Jerusalem) and Gaza
disputes.text: Israel has occupied the West Bank, East Jerusalem and Gaza since the 1967 war. Most countries recognise the State of Palestine, which is a UN observer state, but its borders are not agreed. Israeli settlements in the West Bank are considered illegal under international law by most countries. Gaza has seen major war since October 2023.

disputes.name: Golan Heights
disputes.text: Taken by Israel from Syria in the 1967 war and annexed by Israel in 1981. Almost all countries still consider it Syrian territory occupied by Israel; the United States recognised Israel's claim in 2019.

disputes.name: Crimea
disputes.text: Part of Ukraine, annexed by Russia in 2014 after its troops took control and a referendum that Ukraine and most of the world do not recognise. The UN General Assembly voted that the annexation was invalid.

disputes.name: Eastern and southern Ukraine (Donetsk, Luhansk and beyond)
disputes.text: Russian-backed groups took parts of Donetsk and Luhansk in 2014. Since its full-scale invasion in 2022 Russia has occupied much more of eastern and southern Ukraine, and claims to have annexed four Ukrainian regions (Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson). Ukraine and most countries reject this. The shaded area shows the 2014 lines in Donetsk and Luhansk; the front line has moved since, so check the news for where it is now.

disputes.name: Taiwan
disputes.who: Taiwan (Republic of China) and China (People's Republic of China)
disputes.text: Taiwan has governed itself since 1949, when the losing side of China's civil war moved there, and is a democracy with its own government, army and currency. The People's Republic of China says Taiwan is part of China and has not ruled out force to take it. Only about a dozen countries formally recognise Taiwan, though many, including the UK and US, have close unofficial ties.

disputes.name: Kosovo
disputes.text: Kosovo declared independence from Serbia in 2008, nine years after a war and NATO's intervention. More than 100 countries, including the UK and US, recognise it; Serbia, Russia, China and five EU countries do not, so it is not a UN member.

disputes.name: Northern Cyprus
disputes.who: Cyprus and the Turkish Cypriot north (backed by Turkey)
disputes.text: Turkey's army has held the north of Cyprus since 1974, after a coup backed by Greece's military government. The 'Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus' (declared in 1983) is recognised only by Turkey. A UN buffer zone, the Green Line, divides the island and its capital, Nicosia.

disputes.name: Abkhazia and South Ossetia
disputes.text: Two regions of Georgia that broke away in wars in the early 1990s. After the 2008 Russia–Georgia war, Russia recognised them as independent and keeps troops there; almost every other country considers them part of Georgia, occupied by Russia.

disputes.name: Transnistria
disputes.who: Moldova and a Russian-backed breakaway government
disputes.text: A strip of land along the river Dniester that broke away from Moldova in a short war in 1992. It has its own government, army and currency, and Russian troops are stationed there, but no UN member recognises it.

disputes.name: Nagorno-Karabakh
disputes.text: A mountainous region inside Azerbaijan with a mostly Armenian population, which broke away in a war in 1988–94. Azerbaijan retook land in a 2020 war and the rest in September 2023, when almost all of the 100,000 or so Armenians living there fled to Armenia. The breakaway 'Republic of Artsakh' was dissolved on 1 January 2024. Armenia and Azerbaijan are negotiating a peace treaty.

disputes.name: Somaliland
disputes.text: Declared independence from Somalia in 1991, when Somalia's government collapsed. It has its own elected government, currency and passports and has been far more peaceful than the rest of Somalia, but very few countries recognise it as independent.

disputes.name: Abyei
disputes.text: A small oil-rich area on the border, claimed by both Sudan and South Sudan since South Sudan's independence in 2011. A referendum on which country it should join has never been held; UN peacekeepers are stationed there.

disputes.name: Ilemi Triangle
disputes.text: A dry area of grazing land run by Kenya and claimed by South Sudan, because colonial-era maps drew the border in different places. It matters to the herding peoples who use it.

disputes.name: Kuril Islands (Northern Territories)
disputes.text: The Soviet Union took the four southernmost Kuril Islands from Japan at the end of the Second World War. Japan calls them the Northern Territories and still claims them, so the two countries have never signed a peace treaty.

disputes.name: Falkland Islands (Islas Malvinas)
disputes.text: A British Overseas Territory since 1833, claimed by Argentina, which calls them the Malvinas. Argentina invaded in 1982 and the UK retook the islands in a ten-week war. In a 2013 referendum, 99.8% of islanders voted to stay British.

disputes.name: South China Sea
disputes.who: China, the Philippines, Vietnam, Malaysia, Brunei and Taiwan
disputes.text: China claims most of the sea inside its 'nine-dash line', overlapping the claims of its neighbours to islands, reefs, fishing and the oil and gas under the sea bed. An international tribunal ruled against China's claim in 2016, a ruling China rejects. China has built artificial islands with military bases on reefs in the Spratly Islands.

disputes.name: Essequibo (Guayana Esequiba)
disputes.text: Venezuela claims about two-thirds of Guyana, the land west of the Essequibo River, rejecting a border set by an international tribunal in 1899. The claim became more heated after large oil finds off the coast; the case is at the International Court of Justice.

disputes.name: Border areas claimed by Suriname
disputes.text: Suriname claims two areas of headwaters, one run by Guyana (the New River Triangle) and one by France in French Guiana, because the rivers used as borders in colonial times have more than one source.

disputes.name: Sabah (North Borneo)
disputes.text: Part of Malaysia since 1963. The Philippines has a dormant claim to it, based on the historic Sultanate of Sulu.

disputes.name: Junagadh
disputes.text: A former princely state in Gujarat, India, whose ruler chose to join Pakistan in 1947; India took control and held a referendum that favoured India. Pakistan included it on its official map in 2020. It is run by India.

disputes.name: Senkaku / Diaoyu Islands
disputes.text: Small uninhabited islands run by Japan and claimed by China (as the Diaoyu Islands) and by Taiwan. Chinese coastguard ships regularly enter the waters around them.

conflicts.name: Criminal violence in Haiti
conflicts.text: Armed gangs control most of the capital, Port-au-Prince, and roads across the country; millions of people need food aid and many have fled their homes.

conflicts.name: Criminal violence in Mexico
conflicts.text: Violence between drug cartels, and between the cartels and the state, causes tens of thousands of deaths and disappearances a year.

conflicts.name: Instability in the Northern Triangle
conflicts.text: Gang violence, poverty and weak governments in El Salvador, Guatemala and Honduras push many people to migrate north.

conflicts.name: Instability in Venezuela
conflicts.text: A long political and economic crisis; about 8 million people have left the country since 2014, one of the largest displacements in the world.

conflicts.name: Civil war in Myanmar
conflicts.text: Fighting across the country since the army seized power in a coup in 2021, between the military and many armed opposition and ethnic groups.

conflicts.name: Conflict between Afghanistan and Pakistan
conflicts.text: Border clashes, and attacks by armed groups that Pakistan says operate from Afghanistan, which has been ruled by the Taliban since 2021.

conflicts.name: Conflict between India and Pakistan
conflicts.text: Two nuclear-armed neighbours with a long dispute over Kashmir; there are periodic attacks and military strikes along the Line of Control.

conflicts.name: Confrontation over Taiwan
conflicts.text: China claims Taiwan and holds large military exercises around it; the United States supplies Taiwan with weapons.

conflicts.name: Confrontation with North Korea
conflicts.text: North Korea's nuclear weapons and missile tests cause tension with South Korea, Japan and the United States.

conflicts.name: Territorial disputes in the South China Sea
conflicts.text: Overlapping claims by China and its neighbours to islands, reefs and waters; there are frequent confrontations between ships.

conflicts.name: Tensions between Armenia and Azerbaijan
conflicts.text: After Azerbaijan retook Nagorno-Karabakh in 2023, the two countries have been negotiating a peace treaty.

conflicts.name: War in Ukraine
conflicts.text: Russia's full-scale invasion began in February 2022. Fighting continues mainly in the east and south, with drone and missile attacks across the country; millions of Ukrainians have fled.

conflicts.name: Conflict between Turkey and armed Kurdish groups
conflicts.text: Decades of conflict between Turkey and the PKK, which announced in 2025 that it would disarm and disband.

conflicts.name: Conflict in Yemen and the Red Sea
conflicts.text: A civil war since 2014 that has caused one of the world's worst humanitarian crises. The Houthi movement has attacked ships in the Red Sea, and in September 2026 took the rest of Yemen's Red Sea coast, including the Bab-el-Mandeb strait.

conflicts.name: Conflict with Hezbollah in Lebanon
conflicts.text: Fighting between Israel and Hezbollah, an armed group and political party based in Lebanon.

conflicts.name: War with Iran
conflicts.text: War between Iran and the United States and Israel began in February 2026, after years of confrontation over Iran's nuclear programme. Iran closed or restricted the Strait of Hormuz. A deal to end the war was signed in June, but Iran still limits shipping through the strait and tankers were attacked there in November.

conflicts.name: Instability in Iraq
conflicts.text: Political divisions, armed groups and remaining Islamic State fighters.

conflicts.name: Instability in Libya
conflicts.text: Divided since 2014 between rival governments in the west and the east, each backed by armed groups and foreign powers.

conflicts.name: Instability in Syria
conflicts.text: After 13 years of civil war, the Assad government fell in December 2024; the new government faces violence between communities and armed groups.

conflicts.name: Israeli–Palestinian conflict
conflicts.text: A long conflict over land. War in Gaza began after Hamas attacked Israel on 7 October 2023; tens of thousands of people have been killed and most of Gaza's people forced from their homes.

conflicts.name: Civil war in Sudan
conflicts.text: War since April 2023 between Sudan's army and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces; more than 10 million people have been forced from their homes, and parts of the country face famine.

conflicts.name: Conflict in Ethiopia
conflicts.text: Fighting in the Amhara and Oromia regions, and tension in Tigray, after the 2020–2022 Tigray war.

conflicts.name: Conflict in the Central African Republic
conflicts.text: Armed groups control parts of the country, which has been unstable for most of its history.

conflicts.name: Conflict in the Democratic Republic of Congo
conflicts.text: Fighting in the mineral-rich east between the army and more than 100 armed groups, including M23, which seized the city of Goma in 2025.

conflicts.name: Conflict with al-Shabaab in Somalia
conflicts.text: The government and African Union forces fight al-Shabaab, an armed group linked to al-Qaeda.

conflicts.name: Instability in South Sudan
conflicts.text: Political tension and violence between communities in the world's newest country, which fought a civil war in 2013–2018.

conflicts.name: Violent extremism in the Sahel
conflicts.text: Armed groups linked to al-Qaeda and the Islamic State control large areas of Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger, all now run by military governments.

elections: President (chosen by MPs and state assemblies)
